 Indonesia Prepares Weather Modification Operations To Mitigate Flood Risks In Sumatra
 16/11/2026 08:29 PM 
 Rain Drops -- This image is for illustration purposes only. 
 By Nik Nurfaqih Nik Wil
 JAKARTA, Nov 16 (Bernama) -- Indonesia is preparing to carry out weather modification operations in North Sumatra and Aceh as a precautionary measure to minimise the risk of floods and landslides amid forecasts of heavy rainfall in the coming days.
 National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB) Disaster Data, Information and Communication Centre acting head Berton Panjaitan said 45 subdistricts across 11 regencies and cities in North Sumatra had been placed on alert from Nov 16 to 19, while another 360 subdistricts were under watch.
 He said heavy rain accompanied by thunderstorms was forecast across 19 regencies and cities in North Sumatra during the period. A developing tropical weather system south of Sumatra could also trigger heavy rain and high waves to Aceh, North Sumatra and West Sumatra.
 “As part of efforts to reduce the risk of wet hydrometeorological disasters during the peak of the rainy season in North Sumatra and Aceh, the government through BNPB and the Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG), will conduct weather modification operations.
 “Weather modification does not mean stopping rainfall altogether. These operations are intended to reduce the intensity of rainfall. In simple terms, this redistribution of rainfall aims to reduce moderate or heavy rainfall to light or moderate rainfall,” he said in a statement on Monday.
 Berton said the government was also seeking to accelerate river rehabilitation works in flood-prone areas, particularly in Aceh, to improve water flow and reduce the risk of flooding.
 “The public is urged to remain vigilant as sediment deposits are still accumulating in rivers. Shallow riverbeds can cause rivers to overflow even during light to moderate rainfall. This has also been one of the causes of flooding in several areas of Aceh province,” he said.
